Early Nov 2025 contacted potential supervisor and was encouraged to apply, end of Nov 2025 submitted application, mid Jan 2026 submitted application for L4E fellowship. Early Feb 2026 I get a Whatsapp message from my proposed secondary supervisor on a Sunday afternoon (Montreal time) asking if I'm available in the next couple of hours to discuss my application. As an international applicant in a different time zone unfortunately I was already asleep so replied first thing on Monday morning trying to arrange a time we could talk, and was told they would get back to me with a different time. The next thing I hear is on the 21st April when I get sent an email to look at the application portal where I find a generic rejection message. In the mean time I sent numerous follow up messages asking if they still wanted to talk with me but I never got a reply. McGill's website suggested that most applicants would hear back at the end of February and throughout March so towards the end of March I began to reach out by email to the proposed primary supervisor, program administrator, and L4E to see if they could give me any insight into the progress of my application or when I could expect to hear back. These emails and subsequent follow ups were also all completely ignored. I am obviously gutted about my application being rejected however given the seeming distinct lack of compassion, communication, and organisation shown by the anthropology department at McGill and the L4E it raises some major red flags to me about the quality of teaching and support that is offered by both the program and the fellowship. I would be very interested to hear from successful applicants about if this is the case? If the other applications I am still waiting on are also unsuccessful I will be applying for PhD programs again next year, however given the inadequacy of my experience this year I shan't be reapplying to McGill. Very disappointed.

waitlist for the MFA Program in Creative Writing at The Ohio State University. All of us on the faculty here
greatly admire your work and would be delighted to have you with us next year should a spot open.

15, which is the date by which all admitted students must either decline or accept our offer. It’s very possible
that you will hear from us sooner, but I wouldn’t count on that, as many people wait until the last possible

Comments: For the person who wrote about the prompts and stated that this was unprofessional the process and not to be blindsided, lies. This program is prided on it's multiculturalism which is essentially dealing with culturally linguistically diverse students (which deals with minority students, and you need to know how to deal with all students but also students from diverse population). The prompts are given to see how are thinking are for those scenarios. Clearly, you are a salty person for not getting accepted into the program. Additionally, Queens College has a great reputation for School Psychology. The staff discussed NASP and briefly about their research (which is a lot on multiculturalism). The staff wants to promote a culture where people are not competitive but students who know how to work on a TEAM, which is what this profession is all about. Sorry this program isn't your cup of tea, but don't be salty for not being accepted.

To the responder to the original poster for Quan Methods in Soc Sci. I think you have your head in the clouds. I agree with the original poster- background does matter. I was not putting him down at all. I have no top 100 in my background either. Many of the univesities esp. ivy leagues have cut offs for GRE scores and GPAs to be even in the running. In general, minority students, poor and middle class whites and international students  are relatively disadvantaged both by GREs and by their schools of origen that are typically not in the top tier of U.S. News rankings. Its a crap shoot with weighted dice. Wake up and smell the coffee.

"Your background does not matter, you can do what you set out to do"  Really?  That's awesome!  Because I had to fill out an application with lots of background information - what was I thinking?  Ad coms clearly make decisions from the bottom of their hearts!

To the poster below: Do not belittle him because of his undergrad experiences. All of us do not have the money, family background or the chance to attend the top high schools and Ivy League institutions for undergrad. I applaud him for pushing on. Ivy League or not the graduate admission process is not a level playing field. I did not attend the best, not even ranked in the top 100 program not to mention all black university but I got into many top schools. Do not lose faith and keep sight of your goals. Graduate school admission is a crap shoot. Your background does not matter, you can do what you set out to do; just sometimes the road is a little rougher. Keep pushing on. Keep putting yourself through school, a lot of us have to do just that and once you make it, you will appreciate it much more. Just remember to keep the faith :-)

To the poster below it appears you are being rather nieve about the intense competition in soc sci for an Ivy League school. I would also guess they expect you to have about 700/750 on your GRE quan scores and likely 650 min for verbal, and I imagine community college background was not the best. I'd just be sure not to narrow yourself to ivy league and try to get the best fit for your research interests, and cheer up- may be better program out there for you and there's always next year.

MTEC admissions looks for a well-rounded profile. There is no interview but my guess is that they do care much more than other MSc. of ETH about extracurriculars and the motivation letter. I was top 20% with a 2.3 german grade (nothing that crazy) from a good German uni (mech. eng.), but I frankly had very good extracurriculars (lots of debate, social sciences engagement, formula student, small fintech internship and teaching assistant of 4 subjects, 4 languages). In terms of work experience, I tend to think that they look for potential rather than CV, since I know people with 1, 2 or 3 years of experience in consulting/engineering who got rejected. Ask yourself why this is the right program for you (and not a MiM at HEC Paris for example) and be able to explain it in a good motivation letter. Also, I believe that for masters there is hundreds of chinese and indian students who apply to European unis, which maybe plays against them all, because there is really not a way to differentiate between the top unis in Asia (moral of the story: try to get a well rounded profile rather than focusing your time during the bachelor in being top 1 of the class).

From University of Patras(Greece)-ECE. GPA: 8.56/10, Ranking: 3/250. No publications, no work experience. For all future applicants: You have to put your qualifications into context. Having a GPA of 9/10 means absolutely nothing if there are a lot of students(>10%) with 9/10 or more or if your university does not have many competitive students(ranking does not matter-there are universities that are ranked in a low position globally but attract many good native students). Likewise, in some University systems doing an internship in summer or publishing 2-3 papers before graduating is the norm, while in others it is virtually unheard of. Do not be discouraged if you see other people that seem to have much better qualifications than you do. Not everything that shines is gold, and not all gold shines equally bright. Best of luck to everything you do.
